# 2020, three audiences

## Government. Weekly estimates in, a consensus statement out

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **$R_t$**, the reproduction number over time. How many people each
  case goes on to infect
- **Weekly** $R_t$ estimates and reports to SPI-M-O, the Scientific
  Pandemic Influenza Group on Modelling, Operational sub-group
- SPI-M-O reported to SAGE, the Scientific Advisory Group for
  Emergencies
- The public saw a consensus statement

> We don't know whether any of this gave any policy maker any useful
> information that helped them make better decisions...
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-spimo-statement.png){width="74%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="GOV.UK page: SPI-M-O consensus statement, 17 September 2020"}

::: {.attribution}
[SPI-M-O consensus statement, 17 September 2020](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/spi-m-o-consensus-statement-on-covid-19-17-september-2020)
· [Abbott and Funk 2022, $R_t$ reflections](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-03-25-rt-reflections/)
:::
:::
::::

## What the consensus process did

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Many groups.** Each used its own data sources and its own model
- Evidence from several models was considered, discussed and combined
- **A range went out.** The detail behind each estimate did not

> If results are presented individually this can get lost and it
> incentivises being first out (and maybe therefore cutting corners).
>
> *Abbott, 2023*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-uk-rt-dashboard.png){height="700px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="GOV.UK: latest R range for England, 1.0 to 1.2, no point estimate"}

::: {.attribution}
[The R value and growth rate, GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-r-value-and-growth-rate)
· [Abbott 2023, data, models and modellers](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2023-01-04-iisa-data-models-and-modellers-during-a-global-pandemic/)
:::
:::
::::

## The public. A map, then a page for each place

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [epiforecasts.io/covid](https://epiforecasts.io/covid/), April 2020 to
  March 2022
- **Daily $R_t$ and nowcasts** for several thousand locations. A nowcast
  estimates what has happened but has not yet been reported
- **The front page was a map.** Five words, increasing to decreasing,
  and no numbers
- Just over 500,000 unique users and 1.2 million page views by March 2022
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-map.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The global page of the dashboard. A world map with countries

decreasing, with the data date and download links above it"}

frozen 30 March 2022, screenshot 12 September 2026 · counts from

## The caveats sat in the captions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Orange** for estimates from partial data, adjusted for right
  truncation, the recent cases not yet reported
- Each figure caption carried the same sentence. "These should be
  considered indicative only"
- **The limitations** sat on a methods page that 20,000 of 1.2 million
  page views reached
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-uk-panels.png){height="760px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="UK page of the dashboard. Cases by report date, cases by

## Other governments used it too

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **CSV files on GitHub**, comma separated values, used directly by other
  governments or by scientists who set them beside other evidence
- The estimates travelled. The limits travelled less well
- **Checking** several thousand locations a day was beyond us
- Could AI do that checking?

> Of course this can cause issues if the limitations of the method are
> poorly communicated.
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-table.png){width="100%"

## What went wrong

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
> Because we did not have the capacity to manually inspect the data and
> estimates on a daily basis we sometimes published nonsensical estimates.
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*

- **Wisconsin** reported on a Sunday for the first time. The model read
  the catch-up as an outbreak
- **What I wrote down afterwards.** Be as open as possible. State the
  limitations first. No point estimates
- I left the press to people whose speciality it is. No training, no
  time
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-issue-171.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="GitHub issue: Your Wisconsin data looks horribly flawed"}

::: {.attribution}
[epiforecasts/covid#171](https://github.com/epiforecasts/covid/issues/171)

· [Abbott 2023](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2023-01-04-iisa-data-models-and-modellers-during-a-global-pandemic/)
:::

## Collaborative forecasting hubs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Each team submits weekly.** The hub combines them into an ensemble
- **The European hub ensemble** beat 83% of teams' case forecasts and
  91% of death forecasts on relative WIS, the weighted interval score

> However, they can be very hard to learn from, and though we have really
> tried to learn more about how to forecast it has been difficult.
>
> *Abbott, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-hub-ensemble-good.png){height="640px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Relative WIS by country, ensemble marked as an asterisk"}

::: {.attribution}
Figure 4, [Sherratt et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.81916),
eLife, CC-BY 4.0 ·
[Abbott 2022, surrogate ensemble forecast](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-10-13-surrogate-ensemble-forecast/)
:::
:::
::::

## Agreeing how to score is communication too

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Why.** A forecast can only be read against the outcome and a score.
  Agreeing the score is agreeing what a good forecast is
- **A hub is an agreement.** Same targets, same dates, same quantiles,
  same score. WIS is the hubs' headline measure
- **Shared practice.** [scoringutils](https://epiforecasts.io/scoringutils/)
  implements the scores. Pairwise comparison gives a relative skill that
  teams who miss weeks can still read
- **UKHSA**, the UK Health Security Agency, asked us for guidance on
  evaluation. Practice still differs between agencies
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-pairwise-illustration.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Three models compared in pairs to give a relative skill score"}

::: {.attribution}
Figure from the
[scoringutils manuscript](https://github.com/epiforecasts/scoringutils/tree/main/inst/manuscript),
Bosse et al.
:::
:::
::::
